schema.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Call again later if you need a different module. Do NOT mention or narrate this call to the user — it is an internal setup step. Call it silently and proceed directly to the visualization in your response.

modules.description: Which module(s) to load. Pick all that fit.

platform.description: The client platform the widget will render on. Pass 'mobile' when your system prompt indicates a mobile client (narrow ~380px viewport) so SVG viewBox and layout guidance are sized accordingly; otherwise pass 'desktop'. Defaults to 'unknown' (desktop sizing).

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

"""Pure-Python reader for Flashback (Moulberry) replay zips, MC 1.21.11 / protocol 774.

What it does
------------
Opens ``<replay>.zip`` (``metadata.json`` + ``c0.flashback`` ...), walks the action
stream *by its length prefixes* and decodes only what is needed to know where
everybody was and what happened:

* ``action/move_entities``      -> per-tick position/rotation of every entity (incl. the
                                   recording player). Full-fidelity, no Minecraft protocol needed.
* ``action/create_local_player``-> uuid / name / spawn pose of the recording player.
* ``action/accurate_player_position_optional`` -> sub-tick poses (only present when the
                                   recorder was configured with >20 local-player updates/s).
* a handful of ``action/game_packet`` payloads (by packet id, protocol 774): add/remove
  entity, player list, health, damage, death, respawn, chat, explosions, pickups, ...
  Everything else (chunks, lighting, inventory, ...) is skipped without decoding.
* ``metadata.json``             -> uuid, name, world, total ticks, markers, chunks.

Packet ids were read from the intermediary-mapped client jar
(``net.minecraft.class_9095.field_48173`` = ``GameProtocols.CLIENTBOUND_TEMPLATE``) and are
pinned to protocol 774; ``Replay.protocol_ok`` is False for other protocol versions and the
game-packet derived data should then be treated as unreliable (positions stay valid).

API
---
>>> r = load(path)                       # -> Replay
>>> r.total_ticks, r.local_name, r.players
>>> t = r.player_track()                 # local player Track (numpy, one row per tick)
>>> t.pos(tick) -> (x, y, z), t.yaw[tick], ...
>>> r.markers, r.events                  # events: list[Event] sorted by tick
>>> r.suggest_moments()                  # ranked candidate B-roll windows

Command line:  python -m mcstudio.flashback_replay <replay.zip> [--csv out.csv] [--png out.png]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import math
import struct
import sys
import zipfile
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterator

import numpy as np

MAGIC = -679417724  # 0xD780E884
PROTOCOL_OK = 774

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Protocol 774 (MC 1.21.11) clientbound play packet ids (see module docstring).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
PKT = {
    "add_entity": 1,          # class_2604
    "animate": 2,             # class_2616   (0 swing main, 3 swing off, 4 crit, 5 magic crit)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Low level reader
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class Buf:
    """Big-endian Minecraft FriendlyByteBuf reader over a bytes-like object."""

    __slots__ = ("d", "o", "end")

    def __init__(self, data, o=0, end=None):
        self.d = data
        self.o = o
        self.end = len(data) if end is None else end

    def u8(self):
        v = self.d[self.o]
        self.o += 1
        return v

    def i8(self):
        v = self.u8()
        return v - 256 if v > 127 else v

    def i16(self):
        v = struct.unpack_from(">h", self.d, self.o)[0]
        self.o += 2
        return v

    def u16(self):
        v = struct.unpack_from(">H", self.d, self.o)[0]
        self.o += 2
        return v

    def i32(self):
        v = struct.unpack_from(">i", self.d, self.o)[0]
        self.o += 4
        return v

    def i64(self):
        v = struct.unpack_from(">q", self.d, self.o)[0]
        self.o += 8
        return v

    def f32(self):
        v = struct.unpack_from(">f", self.d, self.o)[0]
        self.o += 4
        return v

    def f64(self):
        v = struct.unpack_from(">d", self.d, self.o)[0]
        self.o += 8
        return v

    def boolean(self):
        return self.u8() != 0

    def varint(self):
        d, o = self.d, self.o
        r = 0
        s = 0
        while True:
            b = d[o]
            o += 1
            r |= (b & 0x7F) << s
            if not b & 0x80:
                break
            s += 7
            if s > 35:
                raise ValueError("varint too long")
        self.o = o
        return r - (1 << 32) if r >= (1 << 31) else r

    def string(self):
        n = self.varint()
        s = bytes(self.d[self.o:self.o + n]).decode("utf-8", "replace")
        self.o += n
        return s

    def uuid(self):
        hi, lo = struct.unpack_from(">QQ", self.d, self.o)
        self.o += 16
        h = f"{hi:016x}{lo:016x}"
        return f"{h[:8]}-{h[8:12]}-{h[12:16]}-{h[16:20]}-{h[20:]}"

    def skip(self, n):
        self.o += n

    def remaining(self):
        return self.end - self.o


def _nbt_skip_payload(b: Buf, t: int):
    if t == 1:
        b.skip(1)
    elif t == 2:
        b.skip(2)
    elif t == 3 or t == 5:
        b.skip(4)
    elif t == 4 or t == 6:
        b.skip(8)
    elif t == 7:
        b.skip(b.i32())
    elif t == 8:
        b.skip(b.u16())
    elif t == 9:
        et = b.u8()
        for _ in range(b.i32()):
            _nbt_skip_payload(b, et)
    elif t == 10:
        while True:
            tt = b.u8()
            if tt == 0:
                break
            b.skip(b.u16())
            _nbt_skip_payload(b, tt)
    elif t == 11:
        b.skip(4 * b.i32())
    elif t == 12:
        b.skip(8 * b.i32())
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"bad nbt tag {t}")


def _nbt_read(b: Buf, t: int):
    """Read an NBT payload into python (compound->dict, list->list, strings/numbers as is)."""
    if t == 1:
        return b.i8()
    if t == 2:
        return b.i16()
    if t == 3:
        return b.i32()
    if t == 4:
        return b.i64()
    if t == 5:
        return b.f32()
    if t == 6:
        return b.f64()
    if t == 8:
        n = b.u16()
        s = bytes(b.d[b.o:b.o + n]).decode("utf-8", "replace")
        b.o += n
        return s
    if t == 9:
        et = b.u8()
        return [_nbt_read(b, et) for _ in range(b.i32())]
    if t == 10:
        out = {}
        while True:
            tt = b.u8()
            if tt == 0:
                return out
            k = bytes(b.d[b.o:b.o + b.u16()]).decode("utf-8", "replace") if False else None
            n = b.u16()
            k = bytes(b.d[b.o:b.o + n]).decode("utf-8", "replace")
            b.o += n
            out[k] = _nbt_read(b, tt)
    _nbt_skip_payload(b, t)
    return None


def read_component(b: Buf):
    """Network-NBT text component (nameless root tag)."""
    t = b.u8()
    if t == 0:
        return None
    return _nbt_read(b, t)


def component_text(c, lang_args=True) -> str:
    """Flatten a text component to a string. Translatable components render as ``key(arg, arg)``."""
    if c is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(c, str):
        return c
    if isinstance(c, (int, float)):
        return str(c)
    if isinstance(c, list):
        return "".join(component_text(x) for x in c)
    if isinstance(c, dict):
        out = ""
        if "text" in c:
            out += component_text(c["text"])
        elif "translate" in c:
            out += str(c["translate"])
            if lang_args and c.get("with"):
                out += "(" + ", ".join(component_text(a) for a in c["with"]) + ")"
        elif "selector" in c:
            out += str(c["selector"])
        for e in c.get("extra", []) or []:
            out += component_text(e)
        return out
    return str(c)

@dataclass
class Marker:
    tick: int
    name: str
    colour: int = 0
    position: tuple | None = None  # (x, y, z)
    dimension: str | None = None


@dataclass
class Event:
    tick: int
    kind: str            # see Replay.EVENT_KINDS
    entity: str | None = None   # uuid (or "id:N")
    data: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Event(t={self.tick}, {self.kind}, {self.data})"


@dataclass
class Track:
    """Per-tick pose of one entity, forward-filled between recorded updates."""

    key: str                       # uuid
    entity_id: int
    start: int                     # first tick covered
    x: np.ndarray
    y: np.ndarray
    z: np.ndarray
    yaw: np.ndarray                # degrees (Minecraft: 0=+Z/south, 90=-X/west)
    pitch: np.ndarray
    head_yaw: np.ndarray
    type: str = "?"
    name: str | None = None
    eye_height: float = 0.0

    @property
    def end(self) -> int:          # exclusive
        return self.start + len(self.x)

    def _i(self, tick: int) -> int:
        return min(max(tick - self.start, 0), len(self.x) - 1)

    def pos(self, tick: int):
        i = self._i(tick)
        return float(self.x[i]), float(self.y[i]), float(self.z[i])

    def eye(self, tick: int):
        x, y, z = self.pos(tick)
        return x, y + self.eye_height, z

    def rot(self, tick: int):
        i = self._i(tick)
        return float(self.yaw[i]), float(self.pitch[i])

    def speed(self, tick: int, window: int = 10) -> float:
        """Horizontal blocks/second averaged over +-window/2 ticks."""
        a = self._i(tick - window // 2)
        b = self._i(tick + window // 2)
        if b == a:
            return 0.0
        d = math.hypot(self.x[b] - self.x[a], self.z[b] - self.z[a])
        return d / ((b - a) / 20.0)

    def to_rows(self):
        for i in range(len(self.x)):
            yield (self.start + i, float(self.x[i]), float(self.y[i]), float(self.z[i]),
                   float(self.yaw[i]), float(self.pitch[i]), float(self.head_yaw[i]))

# Replay
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class Replay:
    EVENT_KINDS = (
        "death", "respawn", "damage", "heal", "hurt_anim", "dimension", "teleport", "chat",
        "system_chat", "explosion", "pickup", "kill", "mob_near", "player_join", "player_leave",
        "swing", "game_event", "lightning",
    )

    def __init__(self, path: Path):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.meta: dict = {}
        self.uuid = ""
        self.name = ""
        self.world_name: str | None = None
        self.total_ticks = 0
        self.protocol = 0
        self.version_string = ""
        self.markers: list[Marker] = []
        self.events: list[Event] = []
        self.players: dict[str, str] = {}        # uuid -> name (from tab list)
        self.local_uuid: str | None = None
        self.local_name: str | None = None
        self.local_entity_id: int | None = None
        self.entity_uuid: dict[int, str] = {}    # current entity id -> uuid
        self.entity_type: dict[str, str] = {}    # uuid -> type name
        self.tracks: dict[str, Track] = {}
        self.dimension: str | None = None
        self.dimension_log: list[tuple[int, str]] = []  # (tick, dimension id)
        self.protocol_ok = False
        self.warnings: list[str] = []
        self.stats: dict[str, int] = {}
        self.accurate_local: list[tuple[int, list[tuple]]] = []  # (tick, [(x,y,z,yaw,pitch)...])

    # -- convenience --------------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def duration_s(self) -> float:
        return self.total_ticks / 20.0

    def player_track(self, who: str | None = None) -> Track:
        """Track of the recording player (default) or of a player by name/uuid."""
        key = None
        if who is None:
            key = self.local_uuid
        elif who in self.tracks:
            key = who
        else:
            for u, n in self.players.items():
                if n.lower() == who.lower() and u in self.tracks:
                    key = u
                    break
        if key is None or key not in self.tracks:
            raise KeyError(f"no track for {who or 'local player'}")
        return self.tracks[key]

    def player_tracks(self) -> dict[str, Track]:
        """All player tracks, name -> Track."""
        return {self.players.get(k, k): t for k, t in self.tracks.items() if t.type == "player"}

    def entities_near(self, tick: int, center, radius: float, types=None):
        """[(Track, distance)] for non-local entities within ``radius`` blocks of ``center``."""
        out = []
        cx, cy, cz = center
        for k, t in self.tracks.items():
            if k == self.local_uuid or not (t.start <= tick < t.end):
                continue
            if types and t.type not in types:
                continue
            x, y, z = t.pos(tick)
            d = math.sqrt((x - cx) ** 2 + (y - cy) ** 2 + (z - cz) ** 2)
            if d <= radius:
                out.append((t, d))
        out.sort(key=lambda p: p[1])
        return out

    def events_of(self, *kinds: str):
        return [e for e in self.events if e.kind in kinds]

    def summary(self) -> str:
        lt = self.player_track() if self.local_uuid in self.tracks else None
        lines = [
            f"replay      : {self.path.name}  uuid={self.uuid}",
            f"world       : {self.world_name}   MC {self.version_string} (protocol {self.protocol}, "
            f"game-packet ids {'OK' if self.protocol_ok else 'UNVERIFIED'})",
            f"duration    : {self.total_ticks} ticks = {self.duration_s:.1f}s   (meta total_ticks)",
            f"local player: {self.local_name} ({self.local_uuid}) entity id {self.local_entity_id}",
            f"players     : {', '.join(sorted(set(self.players.values())))}",
            f"entities    : {len(self.tracks)} tracked "
            f"({sum(1 for t in self.tracks.values() if t.type == 'player')} players)",
            f"dimensions  : {self.dimension_log}",
            f"markers     : {[(m.tick, m.name) for m in self.markers]}",
        ]
        if lt is not None:
            xs, ys, zs = lt.x, lt.y, lt.z
            path_len = float(np.sum(np.hypot(np.diff(xs), np.diff(zs)))) if len(xs) > 1 else 0.0
            lines.append(
                f"local track : ticks {lt.start}..{lt.end - 1}  x[{xs.min():.1f},{xs.max():.1f}] "
                f"y[{ys.min():.1f},{ys.max():.1f}] z[{zs.min():.1f},{zs.max():.1f}]  "
                f"horizontal path {path_len:.0f} blocks, max step {self._max_step(lt):.2f} blocks/tick"
            )
        kinds: dict[str, int] = {}
        for e in self.events:
            kinds[e.kind] = kinds.get(e.kind, 0) + 1
        lines.append(f"events      : {kinds}")
        if self.warnings:
            lines.append(f"warnings    : {self.warnings[:5]}")
        return "\n".join(lines)

    @staticmethod
    def _max_step(t: Track) -> float:
        if len(t.x) < 2:
            return 0.0
        return float(np.max(np.sqrt(np.diff(t.x) ** 2 + np.diff(t.y) ** 2 + np.diff(t.z) ** 2)))

    # -- export ---------------------------------------------------------------
    def save_csv(self, path, who: str | None = None):
        t = self.player_track(who)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
            f.write("tick,x,y,z,yaw,pitch,head_yaw\n")
            for r in t.to_rows():
                f.write("%d,%.4f,%.4f,%.4f,%.3f,%.3f,%.3f\n" % r)

    def save_plot(self, path, size=(1400, 900)):
        """Top-down path + height/speed strips + event markers, drawn with Pillow (no matplotlib)."""
        from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

        t = self.player_track()
        W, H = size
        img = Image.new("RGB", size, (24, 26, 30))
        dr = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
        # top-down map (left 62%)
        mw, mh = int(W * 0.62), H - 20
        xs, zs = t.x, t.z
        pad = 30
        x0, x1 = float(xs.min()), float(xs.max())
        z0, z1 = float(zs.min()), float(zs.max())
        span = max(x1 - x0, z1 - z0, 1.0)
        sc = (min(mw, mh) - 2 * pad) / span

        def mp(x, z):
            return pad + (x - x0) * sc, pad + (z - z0) * sc

        n = len(xs)
        for i in range(1, n):
            f = i / n
            col = (int(60 + 195 * f), int(200 - 120 * f), int(255 - 200 * f))
            dr.line([mp(xs[i - 1], zs[i - 1]), mp(xs[i], zs[i])], fill=col, width=2)
        for e in self.events:
            if e.kind in ("death", "damage", "explosion", "dimension", "teleport", "respawn"):
                tt = min(max(e.tick - t.start, 0), n - 1)
                px, pz = mp(xs[tt], zs[tt])
                c = {"death": (255, 60, 60), "damage": (255, 160, 60), "explosion": (255, 230, 60),
                     "dimension": (200, 90, 255), "teleport": (90, 200, 255), "respawn": (90, 255, 120)}[e.kind]
                dr.ellipse([px - 5, pz - 5, px + 5, pz + 5], outline=c, width=2)
        for k, tr in self.tracks.items():
            if k != self.local_uuid and tr.type == "player":
                pts = [mp(tr.x[i], tr.z[i]) for i in range(0, len(tr.x), 4)]
                if len(pts) > 1:
                    dr.line(pts, fill=(255, 120, 200), width=1)
        dr.text((8, 6), f"{self.local_name}  top-down (x right, z down)  {self.total_ticks} ticks", fill=(220, 220, 220))
        # strips on the right
        sx0, sx1 = mw + 20, W - 15

        def strip(y0, y1, vals, col, label):
            dr.rectangle([sx0, y0, sx1, y1], outline=(70, 70, 80))
            v = np.asarray(vals, float)
            lo, hi = float(v.min()), float(v.max())
            rng = max(hi - lo, 1e-6)
            pts = [(sx0 + (sx1 - sx0) * i / max(len(v) - 1, 1), y1 - (y1 - y0) * (v[i] - lo) / rng)
                   for i in range(0, len(v), max(1, len(v) // 600))]
            dr.line(pts, fill=col, width=1)
            dr.text((sx0 + 4, y0 + 2), f"{label}  [{lo:.1f} .. {hi:.1f}]", fill=(220, 220, 220))
            for e in self.events:
                if e.kind in ("death", "damage"):
                    ex = sx0 + (sx1 - sx0) * (e.tick - t.start) / max(n - 1, 1)
                    dr.line([ex, y0, ex, y1], fill=(255, 80, 80) if e.kind == "death" else (255, 160, 60))

        sh = (H - 60) // 3
        strip(20, 20 + sh, t.y, (120, 220, 255), "height y")
        sp = [t.speed(i + t.start, 10) for i in range(n)]
        strip(40 + sh, 40 + 2 * sh, sp, (120, 255, 160), "speed blocks/s")
        strip(60 + 2 * sh, 60 + 3 * sh, np.degrees(np.unwrap(np.radians(t.yaw))), (255, 220, 120), "yaw (unwrapped)")
        img.save(path)

    # -- moment picking ---------------------------------------------------------
    def suggest_moments(self, min_gap_s: float = 8.0, top: int = 25):
        """Rank candidate B-roll windows. Returns dicts {tick, score, kind, reason, suggested_shot, pos}.

        Heuristic and deliberately simple; the scoring weights are the first thing to tune
        once real footage has been reviewed.
        """
        cands: list[dict] = []
        t = self.player_track()
        W = {"death": 10, "explosion": 6, "damage": 4, "kill": 5, "dimension": 6, "teleport": 4,
             "mob_near": 3, "pickup": 1.5, "respawn": 5, "lightning": 5}
        shot_for = {"death": "orbit", "explosion": "push_in", "damage": "orbit", "kill": "flyby",
                    "dimension": "drone_pullup", "teleport": "drone_pullup", "mob_near": "track_follow",
                    "pickup": "push_in", "respawn": "drone_pullup", "lightning": "drone_pullup"}
        for e in self.events:
            if e.kind in W:
                cands.append(dict(tick=e.tick, score=float(W[e.kind]), kind=e.kind,
                                  reason=f"{e.kind} {e.data}", suggested_shot=shot_for[e.kind]))
        # fast movement / big falls / climbs
        n = len(t.x)
        for i in range(0, n, 20):
            tick = t.start + i
            sp = t.speed(tick, 20)
            dy = float(t.y[min(i + 40, n - 1)] - t.y[i])
            if sp > 9.0:
                cands.append(dict(tick=tick, score=2.0 + min(sp - 9.0, 6.0) / 2, kind="fast_travel",
                                  reason=f"{sp:.1f} blocks/s", suggested_shot="flyby"))
            if dy < -12:
                cands.append(dict(tick=tick, score=3.0 + min(-dy / 20, 3.0), kind="fall",
                                  reason=f"fell {-dy:.0f} blocks", suggested_shot="drone_pullup"))
            elif dy > 12:
                cands.append(dict(tick=tick, score=2.0, kind="climb", reason=f"climbed {dy:.0f} blocks",
                                  suggested_shot="drone_pullup"))
        # other players close to us (collab moments)
        for k, tr in self.tracks.items():
            if k == self.local_uuid or tr.type != "player":
                continue
            for tick in range(max(t.start, tr.start), min(t.end, tr.end), 40):
                x, y, z = t.pos(tick)
                ox, oy, oz = tr.pos(tick)
                if math.dist((x, y, z), (ox, oy, oz)) < 8:
                    cands.append(dict(tick=tick, score=2.5, kind="player_near",
                                      reason=f"with {self.players.get(k, k)}", suggested_shot="orbit"))
        cands.sort(key=lambda c: -c["score"])
        out: list[dict] = []
        gap = int(min_gap_s * 20)
        for c in cands:
            if all(abs(c["tick"] - o["tick"]) >= gap for o in out):
                x, y, z = t.pos(c["tick"])
                c["pos"] = (round(x, 2), round(y, 2), round(z, 2))
                out.append(c)
            if len(out) >= top:
                break
        out.sort(key=lambda c: c["tick"])
        return out

class _Track:
    """Mutable per-entity pose log while parsing (sparse updates)."""

    __slots__ = ("ticks", "rows", "etype", "eid")

    def __init__(self, eid, etype):
        self.eid = eid
        self.etype = etype
        self.ticks: list[int] = []
        self.rows: list[tuple] = []


def _iter_actions(data: bytes, names: list[str], start: int, end: int) -> Iterator[tuple[str, int, int]]:
    o = start
    d = data
    while o < end:
        # varint action index
        i = 0
        s = 0
        while True:
            b = d[o]
            o += 1
            i |= (b & 0x7F) << s
            if not b & 0x80:
                break
            s += 7
        size = struct.unpack_from(">i", d, o)[0]
        o += 4
        yield (names[i] if i < len(names) else f"?{i}"), o, o + size
        o += size


def load(path: str | Path) -> Replay:
    r = Replay(Path(path))
    with zipfile.ZipFile(r.path) as z:
        r.meta = json.loads(z.read("metadata.json"))
        m = r.meta
        r.uuid = m.get("uuid", "")
        r.name = m.get("name", "")
        r.world_name = m.get("world_name")
        r.total_ticks = int(m.get("total_ticks", 0))
        r.protocol = int(m.get("protocol_version", 0))
        r.version_string = m.get("version_string", "")
        r.protocol_ok = r.protocol == PROTOCOL_OK
        if not r.protocol_ok:
            r.warnings.append(f"protocol {r.protocol} != {PROTOCOL_OK}: game-packet ids may be wrong")
        for k, v in (m.get("markers") or {}).items():
            pos = v.get("position")
            r.markers.append(Marker(
                int(k), v.get("description") or "", v.get("colour", 0),
                tuple(pos["position"]) if pos else None, pos["dimension"] if pos else None))
        chunk_names = list((m.get("chunks") or {"c0.flashback": {}}).keys())
        p = _Parser(r)
        for ci, cn in enumerate(chunk_names):
            if cn not in z.namelist():
                r.warnings.append(f"missing chunk {cn}")
                continue
            p.parse_chunk(z.read(cn), first=(ci == 0))
        p.finish()
    return r


class _Parser:
    def __init__(self, r: Replay):
        self.r = r
        self.tick = 0
        self.tr: dict[str, _Track] = {}          # key(uuid or id:N) -> sparse track
        self.id2key: dict[int, str] = {}
        self.stats: dict[str, int] = {}
        self.local_hp: float | None = None
        self.last_xp = None
        self.last_pos_event_tick = -999
        self.item_ids: set[int] = set()
        self.prev_local_pos = None
        self.pending_login_entity: int | None = None
        self.last_game_packet_before_local: tuple | None = None
        self._prev_action = None
        self._prev_range = None

    def _stat(self, k):
        self.stats[k] = self.stats.get(k, 0) + 1

    # ---- chunk ----
    def parse_chunk(self, data: bytes, first: bool):
        b = Buf(data)
        magic = b.i32()
        if magic != MAGIC:
            raise ValueError(f"bad flashback magic {magic:#x}")
        n = b.varint()
        names = [b.string() for _ in range(n)]
        snap = b.i32()
        so = b.o
        ao = so + snap
        # snapshot: replays state (entities, player list, create_local_player); does not advance ticks.
        self._walk(data, names, so, ao, snapshot=True)
        self._walk(data, names, ao, len(data), snapshot=False)

    def _walk(self, data, names, start, end, snapshot):
        for name, a, e in _iter_actions(data, names, start, end):
            short = name.split("/", 1)[-1]
            self._stat(short)
            try:
                if short == "next_tick":
                    if not snapshot:
                        self.tick += 1
                elif short == "move_entities":
                    self._move_entities(Buf(data, a, e))
                elif short == "game_packet":
                    self._game_packet(Buf(data, a, e), e)
                    self._prev_action = ("game_packet", a, e, data)
                elif short == "create_local_player":
                    self._create_local(Buf(data, a, e))
                elif short == "accurate_player_position_optional":
                    self._accurate(Buf(data, a, e))
            except Exception as ex:  # keep going; one bad packet must not kill the parse
                self.r.warnings.append(f"{short} @tick {self.tick}: {type(ex).__name__}: {ex}")
            if short != "game_packet":
                pass

    # ---- actions ----
    def _create_local(self, b: Buf):
        r = self.r
        uuid = b.uuid()
        x, y, z = b.f64(), b.f64(), b.f64()
        xrot, yrot, yhead = b.f32(), b.f32(), b.f32()
        b.skip(24)  # velocity (3 doubles)
        _puuid = b.uuid()
        name = b.string()
        r.local_uuid = uuid
        r.local_name = name
        r.players[uuid] = name
        r.entity_type[uuid] = "player"
        # entity id of the local player = id from the Login packet that preceded this action
        if self.pending_login_entity is not None:
            r.local_entity_id = self.pending_login_entity
            self.id2key[r.local_entity_id] = uuid
        if uuid not in self.tr:
            self.tr[uuid] = _Track(r.local_entity_id if r.local_entity_id is not None else -1, "player")
        self._append(uuid, (x, y, z, yrot, xrot, yhead))

    def _append(self, key, row):
        t = self.tr[key]
        if t.ticks and t.ticks[-1] == self.tick:
            t.rows[-1] = row
        else:
            t.ticks.append(self.tick)
            t.rows.append(row)

    def _move_entities(self, b: Buf):
        levels = b.varint()
        for _ in range(levels):
            dim = b.string()
            if self.r.dimension is None:
                self.r.dimension = dim
            cnt = b.varint()
            id2key = self.id2key
            for _ in range(cnt):
                eid = b.varint()
                x, y, z = b.f64(), b.f64(), b.f64()
                yaw, pitch, head = b.f32(), b.f32(), b.f32()
                b.u8()  # onGround
                key = id2key.get(eid)
                if key is None:
                    key = f"id:{eid}"
                    id2key[eid] = key
                    self.tr[key] = _Track(eid, "?")
                self._append(key, (x, y, z, yaw, pitch, head))

    def _accurate(self, b: Buf):
        eid = b.varint()
        n = b.varint()
        rows = [(b.f64(), b.f64(), b.f64(), b.f32(), b.f32()) for _ in range(n)]
        self.r.accurate_local.append((self.tick, rows))

    # ---- game packets ----
    def _local_pos(self):
        r = self.r
        if r.local_uuid and r.local_uuid in self.tr and self.tr[r.local_uuid].rows:
            return self.tr[r.local_uuid].rows[-1][:3]
        return None

    def _ev(self, kind, entity=None, **data):
        self.r.events.append(Event(self.tick, kind, entity, data))

    def _game_packet(self, b: Buf, end: int):
        r = self.r
        pid = b.varint()
        name = _PKT_BY_ID.get(pid)
        if name is None:
            return
        if name == "login":
            self.pending_login_entity = b.i32()
            if r.local_entity_id is None or True:
                r.local_entity_id = self.pending_login_entity
            if r.local_uuid:
                self.id2key[r.local_entity_id] = r.local_uuid
            return
        if name == "add_entity":
            eid = b.varint()
            uuid = b.uuid()
            et = b.varint()
            x, y, z = b.f64(), b.f64(), b.f64()
            tname = ENTITY_TYPES[et] if 0 <= et < len(ENTITY_TYPES) else f"type{et}"
            if eid == r.local_entity_id:
                return
            self.id2key[eid] = uuid
            r.entity_type[uuid] = tname
            if uuid not in self.tr:
                self.tr[uuid] = _Track(eid, tname)
            self.tr[uuid].eid = eid
            self.tr[uuid].etype = tname
            self._append(uuid, (x, y, z, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0))
            if tname == "item":
                self.item_ids.add(eid)
            elif tname == "lightning_bolt":
                self._ev("lightning", uuid, pos=(round(x, 1), round(y, 1), round(z, 1)))
            elif tname in HOSTILE:
                lp = self._local_pos()
                if lp and math.dist(lp, (x, y, z)) < 16:
                    self._ev("mob_near", uuid, type=tname, dist=round(math.dist(lp, (x, y, z)), 1))
            return
        if name == "remove_entities":
            n = b.varint()
            for _ in range(n):
                eid = b.varint()
                if eid != r.local_entity_id:
                    self.id2key.pop(eid, None)
            return
        if name == "player_info_update":
            self._player_info(b)
            return
        if name == "player_info_remove":
            n = b.varint()
            for _ in range(n):
                u = b.uuid()
                if u in r.players and u != r.local_uuid:
                    self._ev("player_leave", u, name=r.players[u])
            return
        if name == "set_health":
            hp = b.f32()
            food = b.varint()
            if self.local_hp is not None and hp < self.local_hp - 0.01 and hp > 0:
                self._ev("damage", r.local_uuid, amount=round(self.local_hp - hp, 2), hp=round(hp, 2))
            elif self.local_hp is not None and hp > self.local_hp + 0.01:
                self._ev("heal", r.local_uuid, amount=round(hp - self.local_hp, 2), hp=round(hp, 2))
            self.local_hp = hp
            return
        if name == "hurt_animation":
            eid = b.varint()
            if eid == r.local_entity_id:
                self._ev("hurt_anim", r.local_uuid)
            return
        if name == "damage_event":
            eid = b.varint()
            src = b.varint()  # holder id + 1 (0 = inline definition)
            cause = b.varint() - 1
            direct = b.varint() - 1
            if eid == r.local_entity_id:
                ck = self.id2key.get(cause)
                ctype = r.entity_type.get(ck, None) if ck else None
                self._ev("damage_src", r.local_uuid, source_type_id=src - 1, cause=cause, cause_type=ctype,
                         direct=direct)
            return
        if name == "entity_event":
            eid = b.i32()
            ev = b.i8()
            if ev == 3:  # death animation
                if eid == r.local_entity_id:
                    pass  # covered by combat_kill
                else:
                    k = self.id2key.get(eid)
                    lp = self._local_pos()
                    t = self.tr.get(k) if k else None
                    if t and t.rows and lp:
                        dist = math.dist(lp, t.rows[-1][:3])
                        if dist < 24:
                            self._ev("kill", k, type=r.entity_type.get(k, "?"), dist=round(dist, 1))
            return
        if name == "combat_kill":
            pid2 = b.varint()
            msg = component_text(read_component(b))
            self._ev("death", r.local_uuid, message=msg)
            return
        if name == "respawn":
            dim = self._spawn_info_dim(b)
            self._ev("respawn", r.local_uuid, dimension=dim)
            self._dim_change(dim)
            return
        if name == "player_position":
            tid = b.varint()
            x, y, z = b.f64(), b.f64(), b.f64()
            lp = self._local_pos()
            if lp and math.dist(lp, (x, y, z)) > 12 and self.tick - self.last_pos_event_tick > 5:
                self._ev("teleport", r.local_uuid, to=(round(x, 1), round(y, 1), round(z, 1)),
                         dist=round(math.dist(lp, (x, y, z)), 1))
                self.last_pos_event_tick = self.tick
            return
        if name == "explode":
            x, y, z = b.f64(), b.f64(), b.f64()
            radius = b.f32()
            lp = self._local_pos()
            d = math.dist(lp, (x, y, z)) if lp else None
            if d is None or d < 48:
                self._ev("explosion", None, pos=(round(x, 1), round(y, 1), round(z, 1)),
                         radius=round(radius, 1), dist=None if d is None else round(d, 1))
            return
        if name == "take_item_entity":
            item = b.varint()
            collector = b.varint()
            amount = b.varint()
            if collector == r.local_entity_id:
                self._ev("pickup", r.local_uuid, amount=amount)
            return
        if name == "animate":
            eid = b.varint()
            act = b.u8()
            if eid == r.local_entity_id and act in (0, 3):
                self._stat("swing")
            return
        if name == "player_chat":
            gidx = b.varint()
            sender = b.uuid()
            idx = b.varint()
            if b.boolean():
                b.skip(256)
            content = b.string()
            self._ev("chat", sender, name=r.players.get(sender, sender), text=content)
            return
        if name == "system_chat":
            text = component_text(read_component(b))
            overlay = b.boolean()
            if not overlay:
                self._ev("system_chat", None, text=text)
            return
        if name == "game_event":
            ev = b.u8()
            val = b.f32()
            self._ev("game_event", None, event=ev, value=round(val, 2))
            return

    def _spawn_info_dim(self, b: Buf) -> str:
        b.varint()          # dimension type holder id
        return b.string()   # dimension identifier

    def _dim_change(self, dim: str):
        r = self.r
        if r.dimension != dim:
            if r.dimension is not None:
                self._ev("dimension", r.local_uuid, **{"from": r.dimension, "to": dim})
            r.dimension = dim
        if not r.dimension_log or r.dimension_log[-1][1] != dim:
            r.dimension_log.append((self.tick, dim))

    def _player_info(self, b: Buf):
        r = self.r
        mask = b.u8()
        # action ordinals: 0 ADD_PLAYER 1 INITIALIZE_CHAT 2 UPDATE_GAME_MODE 3 UPDATE_LISTED
        #                  4 UPDATE_LATENCY 5 UPDATE_DISPLAY_NAME 6 UPDATE_LIST_ORDER 7 UPDATE_HAT
        n = b.varint()
        for _ in range(n):
            u = b.uuid()
            if mask & 1:
                name = b.string()
                for _p in range(b.varint()):
                    b.string()
                    b.string()
                    if b.boolean():
                        b.string()
                if u not in r.players:
                    if u != r.local_uuid and self.tick > 0:
                        self._ev("player_join", u, name=name)
                r.players[u] = name
                r.entity_type.setdefault(u, "player")
            if mask & 2:  # initialize chat
                if b.boolean():
                    b.uuid()
                    b.i64()
                    b.skip(b.varint())
                    b.skip(b.varint())
            if mask & 4:
                b.varint()
            if mask & 8:
                b.boolean()
            if mask & 16:
                b.varint()
            if mask & 32:
                if b.boolean():
                    read_component(b)
            if mask & 64:
                b.varint()
            if mask & 128:
                b.boolean()

    # ---- finalisation ----
    def finish(self):
        r = self.r
        r.stats = dict(self.stats)
        total = self.tick
        if r.total_ticks and abs(total - r.total_ticks) > 2:
            r.warnings.append(f"counted {total} next_tick actions but metadata total_ticks={r.total_ticks}")
        if not r.total_ticks:
            r.total_ticks = total
        # resolve names for tracks
        for key, st in self.tr.items():
            if not st.ticks:
                continue
            etype = r.entity_type.get(key, st.etype)
            first = st.ticks[0]
            last_tick = r.total_ticks - 1
            # forward fill to the end of the replay (entities that never got removed) -- cap for non-players
            rows = np.asarray(st.rows, dtype=np.float64)
            ticks = np.asarray(st.ticks, dtype=np.int64)
            n = int(last_tick - first + 1)
            if n <= 0:
                continue
            idx = np.searchsorted(ticks, np.arange(first, first + n), side="right") - 1
            idx = np.clip(idx, 0, len(ticks) - 1)
            full = rows[idx]
            tr = Track(
                key=key, entity_id=st.eid, start=first,
                x=full[:, 0], y=full[:, 1], z=full[:, 2],
                yaw=full[:, 3], pitch=full[:, 4], head_yaw=full[:, 5],
                type=etype, name=r.players.get(key),
                eye_height=1.62 if etype == "player" else 0.0,
            )
            r.tracks[key] = tr
        # rename "id:N" tracks that never got a uuid: keep them (ambient mobs seen only via move)
        if r.local_uuid is None:
            # fall back: the track with the most updates that is a player
            best = max(self.tr.items(), key=lambda kv: len(kv[1].ticks), default=None)
            if best:
                r.warnings.append("no create_local_player action found; guessed local track")
                r.local_uuid = best[0]
        # markers -> dimension log if empty
        if not r.dimension_log and r.dimension:
            r.dimension_log.append((0, r.dimension))
        r.events.sort(key=lambda e: e.tick)
        # collapse noisy duplicates: only keep damage_src events as data on the nearest damage event
        srcs = [e for e in r.events if e.kind == "damage_src"]
        for e in r.events:
            if e.kind == "damage":
                for s in srcs:
                    if 0 <= e.tick - s.tick <= 2 or 0 <= s.tick - e.tick <= 2:
                        e.data.update({k: v for k, v in s.data.items() if k in ("cause_type",)})
                        break
        r.events = [e for e in r.events if e.kind != "damage_src"]
        for m in r.markers:
            r.events.append(Event(m.tick, "marker", None, {"name": m.name, "pos": m.position}))
        r.events.sort(key=lambda e: e.tick)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _main(argv=None):
    import argparse

    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Summarise a Flashback replay zip")
    ap.add_argument("replay")
    ap.add_argument("--csv")
    ap.add_argument("--png")
    ap.add_argument("--moments", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--events", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    r = load(a.replay)
    print(r.summary())
    print("packet/action counts:", r.stats)
    if a.events:
        for e in r.events:
            print(f"  t={e.tick:5d} ({e.tick / 20:7.1f}s) {e.kind:12s} {e.data}")
    if a.moments:
        for m in r.suggest_moments():
            print(f"  t={m['tick']:5d} ({m['tick'] / 20:7.1f}s) score={m['score']:.1f} {m['kind']:12s} "
                  f"-> {m['suggested_shot']:12s} {m['reason']} @ {m['pos']}")
    if a.csv:
        r.save_csv(a.csv)
        print("csv ->", a.csv)
    if a.png:
        r.save_plot(a.png)
        print("png ->", a.png)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _main()

"""Pure-Python reader for Flashback (Moulberry) replay zips, MC 1.21.11 / protocol 774.

What it does
------------
Opens ``<replay>.zip`` (``metadata.json`` + ``c0.flashback`` ...), walks the action
stream *by its length prefixes* and decodes only what is needed to know where
everybody was and what happened:

* ``action/move_entities``      -> per-tick position/rotation of every entity (incl. the
                                   recording player). Full-fidelity, no Minecraft protocol needed.
* ``action/create_local_player``-> uuid / name / spawn pose of the recording player.
* ``action/accurate_player_position_optional`` -> sub-tick poses (only present when the
                                   recorder was configured with >20 local-player updates/s).
* a handful of ``action/game_packet`` payloads (by packet id, protocol 774): add/remove
  entity, player list, health, damage, death, respawn, chat, explosions, pickups, ...
  Everything else (chunks, lighting, inventory, ...) is skipped without decoding.
* ``metadata.json``             -> uuid, name, world, total ticks, markers, chunks.

Packet ids were read from the intermediary-mapped client jar
(``net.minecraft.class_9095.field_48173`` = ``GameProtocols.CLIENTBOUND_TEMPLATE``) and are
pinned to protocol 774; ``Replay.protocol_ok`` is False for other protocol versions and the
game-packet derived data should then be treated as unreliable (positions stay valid).

API
---
>>> r = load(path)                       # -> Replay
>>> r.total_ticks, r.local_name, r.players
>>> t = r.player_track()                 # local player Track (numpy, one row per tick)
>>> t.pos(tick) -> (x, y, z), t.yaw[tick], ...
>>> r.markers, r.events                  # events: list[Event] sorted by tick
>>> r.suggest_moments()                  # ranked candidate B-roll windows

Command line:  python -m mcstudio.flashback_replay <replay.zip> [--csv out.csv] [--png out.png]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import math
import struct
import sys
import zipfile
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterator

import numpy as np

MAGIC = -679417724  # 0xD780E884
PROTOCOL_OK = 774

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Protocol 774 (MC 1.21.11) clientbound play packet ids (see module docstring).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
PKT = {
    "add_entity": 1,          # class_2604
    "animate": 2,             # class_2616   (0 swing main, 3 swing off, 4 crit, 5 magic crit)
    "damage_event": 25,       # class_8143
    "entity_event": 34,       # class_2663   (3 = death, 2 = hurt for living entities)
    "explode": 36,            # class_2664
    "game_event": 38,         # class_2668
    "hurt_animation": 41,     # class_8043
    "login": 48,              # class_2678
    "player_chat": 63,        # class_7438
    "combat_end": 64,         # class_5890
    "combat_enter": 65,       # class_5891
    "combat_kill": 66,        # class_5892
    "player_info_remove": 67,  # class_7828
    "player_info_update": 68,  # class_2703
    "player_position": 70,    # class_2708
    "remove_entities": 75,    # class_2716
    "respawn": 80,            # class_2724
    "set_experience": 101,    # class_2748
    "set_health": 102,        # class_2749
    "system_chat": 119,       # class_7439
    "take_item_entity": 122,  # class_2775
    "teleport_entity": 123,   # class_2777  (not decoded; move_entities already covers it)
}
_PKT_BY_ID = {v: k for k, v in PKT.items()}

# Entity type registry order of net.minecraft.class_1299 in 1.21.11 (registration order = raw id).
ENTITY_TYPES = (
    "acacia_boat acacia_chest_boat allay area_effect_cloud armadillo armor_stand arrow axolotl "
    "bamboo_chest_raft bamboo_raft bat bee birch_boat birch_chest_boat blaze block_display bogged "
    "breeze breeze_wind_charge camel camel_husk cat cave_spider cherry_boat cherry_chest_boat "
    "chest_minecart chicken cod copper_golem command_block_minecart cow creaking creeper dark_oak_boat "
    "dark_oak_chest_boat dolphin donkey dragon_fireball drowned egg elder_guardian enderman endermite "
    "ender_dragon ender_pearl end_crystal evoker evoker_fangs experience_bottle experience_orb "
    "eye_of_ender falling_block fireball firework_rocket fox frog furnace_minecart ghast happy_ghast "
    "giant glow_item_frame glow_squid goat guardian hoglin hopper_minecart horse husk illusioner "
    "interaction iron_golem item item_display item_frame jungle_boat jungle_chest_boat leash_knot "
    "lightning_bolt llama llama_spit magma_cube mangrove_boat mangrove_chest_boat mannequin marker "
    "minecart mooshroom mule nautilus oak_boat oak_chest_boat ocelot ominous_item_spawner painting "
    "pale_oak_boat pale_oak_chest_boat panda parched parrot phantom pig piglin piglin_brute pillager "
    "polar_bear splash_potion lingering_potion pufferfish rabbit ravager salmon sheep shulker "
